uzo.purpose: Switches between views of the same thing on one page: content, versions, rules, audit.

instead.kialo: A choice in a form is a value, not a switch of views, because it is sent with the form and read back as data; that is the elekto.
Pages of an application are a navigation, because the person leaves where they are; tabs switch views of one thing and stay on the page.
Content that is hidden until opened is a disclosure, because tabs always show one view; the faldilo opens and closes, several in a group one at a time.
The pages of one long list are a pagination, because the person moves through parts of the same list in order; tabs switch views of one thing.

boundary.kialo: More tabs than the line holds need a rule for what happens to the rest (a second line, a scroll, a list), because every rule hides something; a person decides which.
A tab a person can close is a document, not a view of one thing, because closing it removes content; Fundamento has no such tab.
Selection follows the focus here (automatic activation), because a panel that is cheap to show should show at once; a panel that is slow to load wants Enter to select, which a person decides.
Tabs along the side read like a navigation, because a column of places is what a sidebar is; a person decides whether these are views of one thing or pages.

containers.name: page-section
containers.kialo: Tabs head a section of the page, because the views they switch belong to that section's one thing.
